jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer — Distributed Systems & Real-Time APIs
jobs.description:
Plantra Labs builds the infrastructure behind intelligent products. We are seeking a Senior Backend Engineer to design and scale the distributed event pipelines, transactional services, and ultra-low-latency APIs that power our real-time AI platform.

In this role, you will lead the architecture of high-throughput backend microservices handling millions of concurrent WebSocket events, streaming audio frames, and distributed transactional state. You will work closely with our AI Systems and Core Platform teams to deliver resilient, sub-50ms p99 response times across our global edge network.

Key Responsibilities:
• Architect, deploy, and scale high-concurrency backend services in TypeScript/Node.js and Go across containerized Kubernetes clusters.
• Design high-throughput, fault-tolerant event ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka, Redis Pub/Sub, and PostgreSQL connection pooling.
• Optimize database schemas, query plans, indexing strategies, and distributed cache invalidation layers.
• Implement end-to-end distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), health checks, and automated failover mechanics for mission-critical customer workloads.
• Define API contracts, collaborate with frontend and ML engineers on streaming payload schemas, and drive engineering best practices.
jobs.requirements:
Required Qualifications:
• 3”“6 years of professional backend engineering experience building and scaling distributed systems in production.
• Strong proficiency in TypeScript, Node.js, and/or Go, with deep understanding of asynchronous event loops, non-blocking I/O, and concurrency patterns.
• Deep hands-on experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL indexing, query optimization, connection pooling) and caching layers (Redis).
• Proven experience designing high-throughput, low-latency REST and WebSocket APIs under strict SLAs.
• Strong understanding of distributed systems principles: CAP theorem, eventual consistency, partition tolerance, and idempotent operations.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with event streaming architectures using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, or AWS Kinesis.
• Familiarity with containerized deployments on Kubernetes (EKS/GKE) and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).
• Prior experience with real-time media transport (WebRTC) or streaming LLM inference gateways.

jobs.title: Staff Backend Engineer — Core Infrastructure & Architecture
jobs.description:
As a Staff Backend Engineer at Plantra Labs, you will serve as a principal technical leader shaping the next generation of our global AI infrastructure. You will own the technical roadmap for our high-concurrency orchestration platform, multi-region database replication, and real-time inference streaming pipelines.

You will tackle some of our hardest distributed systems challenges: multi-region active-active failover, microsecond-level serialization overhead, state machine synchronization across edge clusters, and zero-downtime database schema migrations.

Key Responsibilities:
• Lead architectural strategy and technical standards across Plantra's distributed backend services and data infrastructure.
• Design resilient multi-region architectures supporting 10x traffic growth with 99.99% availability SLAs.
• Champion high-performance concurrency patterns, memory profiling, and network optimization across Go and Node.js microservices.
• Mentor senior engineers, author detailed technical RFCs, and establish engineering guidelines for latency budgets and fault containment.
• Partner with product management and executive leadership to align infrastructure investments with enterprise platform capabilities.
jobs.requirements:
Required Qualifications:
• 7+ years of software engineering experience with demonstrated technical leadership in large-scale distributed systems.
• Deep expertise in distributed systems architecture, event-driven topologies, consensus mechanisms (Raft/Paxos), and high-throughput streaming.
• Mastery of concurrency, memory management, and performance profiling in Go, TypeScript/Node.js, or Rust.
• Extensive experience scaling PostgreSQL, distributed key-value stores (Redis clusters), and messaging systems (Kafka) to billions of monthly events.
• Track record of driving complex architectural initiatives from conception to multi-region production rollout.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience designing mission-critical developer platforms or real-time communication backbones.
• Expertise in multi-region Kubernetes deployments, service mesh architectures (Istio/Envoy), and disaster recovery design.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience publishing technical RFCs.

jobs.title: AI / Machine Learning Engineer — Conversational Systems & LLM Infra
jobs.description:
At Plantra Labs, our AI Platform team researches, evaluates, and deploys the intelligence models that power our multi-persona conversational agents and autonomous evaluation engines. We are seeking an AI/ML Engineer to push the boundaries of real-time conversational agents, streaming speech-to-speech pipelines, and grounded LLM evaluation.

You will work on low-latency inference orchestration (vLLM/TensorRT-LLM), multi-agent floor arbitration, hallucination guardrails, and retrieval-augmented synthesis pipelines.

Key Responsibilities:
• Design, evaluate, and deploy fine-tuned LLMs and multimodal agent pipelines tailored for specialized conversational personas.
• Optimize real-time streaming audio intelligence pipelines integrating streaming ASR, low-latency LLM generation, and neural TTS.
• Build grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows with semantic vector search, context caching, and factual verification.
• Develop automated multi-round evaluation rubrics with calibrated confidence scoring and bias mitigation metrics.
• Benchmark inference throughput and time-to-first-token (TTFT) across GPU compute clusters.
jobs.requirements:
Required Qualifications:
• 2”“5 years of hands-on experience building, fine-tuning, and evaluating production ML models and LLM systems.
• Strong proficiency in Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, and modern ML engineering tooling.
• Deep understanding of LLM architectures, prompt engineering, few-shot grounding, and RAG retrieval pipelines.
• Solid foundation in machine learning system design, evaluation methodology, and metrics formulation.
• Experience with vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector) and embedding models.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with real-time conversational agents, voice/audio AI models, or full-duplex speech systems.
• Hands-on experience with LLM serving engines (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server).
• Prior contributions to open-source AI frameworks or published research in NLP/Conversational AI.

jobs.title: Senior Platform Engineer — Cloud Infrastructure & Kubernetes
jobs.description:

You will own Kubernetes fleet management, GPU node autoscaling, Terraform Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD automation, and zero-trust security baselines across our global infrastructure.

• Automate cloud networking, VPC peering, global load balancing, and edge CDN routing for sub-50ms latency.
• Ensure enterprise-grade security hardening, KMS encryption, automated vulnerability patching, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 compliance.

• Hands-on experience implementing SOC 2 Type II compliance controls and automated security scanning.
• Experience with multi-region active-active architectures and disaster recovery testing.

transcript.speaker: Priya Sharma (Principal Architect)
transcript.text: Can you walk us through your algorithmic approach and time complexity for the sliding window solution?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I used a two-pointer dynamic sliding window with character frequency hash maps. As the right pointer expands, we record frequencies until all distinct target characters are matched. Then we contract from the left to find the minimal valid window. Both expansion and contraction visit each character at most twice, achieving strict O(N + M) linear time complexity with O(k) auxiliary space where k is the character alphabet size.

transcript.speaker: Arjun Mehta (Lead Systems Engineer)
transcript.text: In your resume you mention handling high-concurrency event streams with Apache Kafka and Redis caching. How did you handle consumer group rebalances and avoid message duplication during network partitions?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: We used cooperative sticky partition assignment to minimize stop-the-world rebalance pauses across consumer instances. For duplicate prevention, we implemented idempotent consumer processing using distributed Redis locks keyed on unique event idempotency keys with a 10-minute TTL, combined with database unique constraints on our PostgreSQL event outbox table. When partitions occurred, backpressure was managed via reactive Kafka stream pauses rather than crashing worker pods.

transcript.text: We selected eventual consistency for read-heavy query endpoints backed by distributed Redis clusters, while maintaining linearizable consistency on transactional writes via PostgreSQL two-phase commits with read-after-write session tokens for updated user accounts.

transcript.text: In my previous role at Stripe, we had a major architectural disagreement regarding database migration to DynamoDB. We delivered the migration on schedule with 100% uptime and the team adopted our shadow verification protocol for all future service splits.

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: At Datadog, I led the distributed tracing ingest pipeline migration across 4 cross-functional squads. When two senior engineers vehemently disagreed on whether to use Apache Pulsar vs Kafka Streams, I designed an objective decision matrix measuring end-to-end tail latency, operational complexity, and partition rebalancing overhead. We ran parallel staging load tests simulating 500k events/sec. When the benchmarks demonstrated Kafka Streams had 40% lower P99 latency and our SRE team was already certified in Kafka operations, the team achieved unanimous alignment. The migration was completed 2 weeks ahead of Q3 deadline with zero customer incidents.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: Welcome to Round 1! Walk me through your rate limiter.

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I implemented an in-memory sliding window rate limiter using a Hash Map that stores request timestamps per user ID. For every request, we filter out timestamps outside the current window in O(N) where N is max allowed requests per window, ensuring average O(1) operational overhead and O(U * N) space complexity across unique users.

transcript.speaker: Priya Nair
transcript.text: How do you handle partition tolerance and consistency in high-scale distributed systems?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: In our payment ingestion pipeline handling 80,000 TPS, we adopted a tunable consistency model. We partitioned transactions by account ID using consistent hashing with virtual nodes on Kafka topics. For idempotency and double-spend prevention, we implemented distributed optimistic locking backed by Redis distributed locks with Redlock algorithm and Postgres serializable snapshot isolation. When network partitions occurred, we favored consistency (CP) for balances while maintaining AP availability for read-only statement queries with read replicas and asynchronous change-data-capture via Debezium.

transcript.speaker: Arjun Mehta
transcript.text: What happens when the leader node crashes during a 2-phase commit?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: To avoid 2PC coordinator crash deadlocks, we replaced 2PC with a Saga orchestration pattern with compensating transactions and outbox event streaming. Every transaction state transition writes to an immutable transactional outbox table in Postgres in the exact same ACID transaction as the state update, polled by a Debezium CDC connector publishing to partitioned Kafka topics with dead letter queue retries and exponential jitter backoff.
